The President/Chairman of African Legacy Media Services Limited and member of the Organising Committee, Engr Innocent Ogu, said the initiative would give outstanding students national recognition. He said it would also celebrate the contributions of parents, teachers and schools to their achievements. Ogu said the programme went beyond presenting awards, as it would promote merit, encourage hard work and strengthen the value of education. He said, “Every outstanding student deserves encouragement, every dedicated teacher deserves recognition, and every child deserves to see that excellence can open doors to opportunity and a greater future.” The organisers said the programme would celebrate exceptional academic performances, promote positive role models and encourage investment in education and youth development. He called on government agencies, state governments, educational institutions, corporate organisations and development partners to support the initiative, while urging the media to publicise the achievements and inspiring stories of the students through newspapers, television, radio and online platforms. The 2026 Presidential Prize-Giving Day will be officially unveiled on Friday, 4 December, at the Federal Ministry of Education, Federal Secretariat Complex, Abuja. The grand award ceremony is scheduled for Friday, 18 December, at Abuja Continental Hotel, Abuja. The organisers noted that the grand ceremony is expected to attract outstanding students, parents, school representatives, government officials, education stakeholders and corporate organisations.
